name: Kassák Múzeum
known: Directors: Ferenc Csaplár (1976 to 2006), Gábor Andrási (2006 to 2010), Edit Sasvári (2010 to 2020) and Merse Pál Szeredi (2020 to the present).

name: Ludwig Museum Budapest
known: Founded by the German collectors Peter and Irene Ludwig: the contract to establish it was signed in Budapest on 21 March 1989, and the Ludwig Foundation donated 70 artworks to the state of Hungary to establish the collection (Ludwig Museum).
The director is Júlia Fabényi (Ludwig Museum website;

name: Museum of Fine Arts Budapest / Hungarian National Gallery
known: USA Art News (2026) calls him director general of it and the National Gallery.
In April 2026 director László Baán quit the National Cultural Fund committee, saying many grants did not fit its aims.

name: Trafó House of Contemporary Arts
known: Directors: György Szabó (1998 to 2012), József Nagy (2012 to 2017), Beáta Barda (2017 to 2024), Katalin Erdődi (2025 to 2026) (Hungarian Wikipedia).

Managing director György Szabó said in an interview published on 29 December 2014 that Trafó receives state funding, which gives it a known annual budget, "a better situation than the independent theatres" (Anna Frenyó, Heinrich Böll Stiftung).

name: Walter Rózsi Villa
known: Under first head György Fekete the Academy took over the Műcsarnok-Kunsthalle in 2013 and named György Szegő its art director in 2014 (Artistic Freedom Initiative).

name: Kling & Bang
known: The article also names Hekla Dögg Jónsdóttir and Guðmundur Oddur Magnússon as founders of Klink and Bank.

TBA21 (Thyssen-Bornemisza Art Contemporary): its page says it is supporting Kling & Bang's annual curatorial programme; in 2013 TBA21 and Kling & Bang collaborated on bringing Ragnar Kjartansson's "The Visitors" to the gallery (TBA21 page).

The National Bank of Iceland, which approached the gallery in November 2003, funded the Klink and Bank conversion; founder Erling Klingenberg recalls that the bank's only proviso was that the artists run it responsibly.

name: 1 Shanthiroad Studio Gallery
known: Founded by Suresh Jayaram, a professor of art history and later dean at Karnataka Chitrakala Parishad from 1993 to 2007 (Temporary Art Review, 2015).

Project funding: a 2012 curatorial residency at the space was part of the Curatorship Programme, run by Khoj and conceptualised by the India Foundation for the Arts; the Khoj call says "The Curatorship Programme is funded by the Jamsetji Tata Trust".

name: Kochi-Muziris Biennale
known: The sixth edition, "For the Time Being", curated by Nikhil Chopra with HH Art Spaces, ran from 12 December 2025 to 31 March 2026 (Kerala Chief Minister's announcement via The Week; e-flux).
The seventh, in 2027 to 2028, is curated by Kader Attia (stated by the Biennale).
Chairperson Venu Vasudevan said he could not give further details (Onmanorama, 14 January 2026).
The Week's 2024 report named V Venu as the new Foundation chairperson.

2025 to 2026: philanthropist Minal Bajaj, trustee and Honorary Director of the Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation since 2009, is a Platinum Patron of the sixth edition; the Biennale's own news item of 11 December 2025 gives no amount.
Founder Bose Krishnamachari resigned in January 2026.

name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Mumbai City Museum
known: It won the 2005 UNESCO Asia-Pacific Award of Excellence in Cultural Conservation.
Tasneem Zakaria Mehta is honorary director and the board includes the mayor and municipal commissioner (Wikipedia).
Names its Board of Trustees, chaired by the Mumbai mayor.

name: Jehangir Art Gallery
known: The committee chairman is Adi H.
The gallery names its management committee with chairman Adi Jehangir.

name: Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC)
known: Opened on 31 March 2023, founded by Nita Ambani, chairperson of Reliance Foundation.
Its opening shows were "Sangam/Confluence", curated by Ranjit Hoskote and Jeffrey Deitch, and "India in Fashion".
"Pop: Fame, Love, Power" ran until 11 February 2024, curated by collector and dealer Lawrence Van Hagen, with loans including works from Isha Ambani Piramal.
Nita Ambani is the foundation's founder-chairperson (The Established).

name: Khoj International Artists' Association
known: The founding working group was Ajay Desai, Anita Dube, Bharti Kher, Subodh Gupta, Prithpal Singh Ladi, Manisha Parekh and Pooja Sood, and Sood is currently its director (Wikipedia).
Khoj's story page says the idea began as "a gift of possibility given by Robert Loder", founder of the Triangle Arts Trust.

Programmes (Khoj's story page): the South Asia Network for the Arts (initiated 2001), the Peers student residency (from 2003), Curatorial Intensive South Asia (from 2017) and the Khoj Support Grant (from 2020).
Khoj began in 1997 with Triangle Arts Trust, set up the South Asian Network for the Arts in 2004 with Vasl and others, and co-runs a curatorial programme with Goethe-Institut.
